design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


An explicit, first-class abstraction for transitions between thermodynamic
interpretations, with spec, result and report types.

**Do not hide the bridge inside arbitrary unit-operation code.**

A user should be able to write approximately:

```rust
let outlet = inlet.reinterpret(&electrolyte_package, BridgeSpec::PH)?;
```

or have the solver perform the transition when connecting incompatible units.
Advanced users must still be able to instantiate and inspect bridge objects
explicitly.

## Naming — resolve this first

**`columns/thermo_bridge.rs` already exists** and is a different thing: a shim
mapping DWSIM's rigorous-column property-package calls (`DW_CalcKvalue`,
`DW_CalcEnthalpy`, `Flash_PV`) onto this crate's thermo kernel. Reusing
`ThermoBridge` for package transitions collides with a well-documented existing
module. **Choose a distinct name, or rename the existing one, deliberately and
before code is written.**

Consider whether `StreamSpec` (already carrying TP/PH/PS/PVF) should be the
bridge specification rather than a parallel enum.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Bridge API: the core abstraction

description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, second comment). Depends on op-63u0 (design spec must exist first).

SCOPE: library + CLI/GUI-triggerable logic that scans a 'kovan folder' (pdf/, markdown/, the user's .bib) and writes/refreshes kovan.toml per op-63u0's spec -- one entry per document pointing to its bib entry, PDF path, markdown path, and the line-number ranges of each standard markdown section (AI summary, author summary, full text, table CSVs, graph CSVs). Regenerates automatically whenever a tracked markdown file changes, per the design bead's regeneration-trigger decision.

Not a hand-authored file -- see op-63u0's reconciliation with docs/kovan.md's 'only the Rust struct is authoritative' rule.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented: new crates/kovan/src/project.rs library module (ProjectIndex/DocumentEntry/SectionRanges schema, scan_markdown_sections marker scanner, regenerate/write_index/regenerate_and_write) implementing the design in docs/kovan-folder-format.md (op-63u0) sections 3/4.1/5. Wired as kovan-cli project regen <path>, printing one line per indexed document then a summary. kovan.toml is written atomically (temp file + rename) with a 'GENERATED FILE -- do not edit by hand' header per the design doc's reconciliation with docs/kovan.md's canonical-representation rule.

KNOWN, DOCUMENTED V1 SCOPING LIMITATION (flagged in the module's own doc comment, not silently done): the design doc says document.id must equal the .bib entry's cite key, but this workspace has no BibTeX PARSER (kovan_literature::bibtex::to_bibtex only renders KovanDocument -> BibTeX, one-way). regenerate() instead joins pdf/<stem>.pdf with markdown/<stem>.md by shared filename stem and uses the stem as id. This is an honest, working v1, not the bib-key join the design doc describes -- closing the gap needs a BibTeX parser somewhere in the workspace first (kovan-literature is the natural home). Filing as a follow-up bead now.

Verified: 8 new unit tests (marker scanning incl. missing/duplicate/unknown-section error paths, TOML round-trip, full synthetic-project regenerate+write+reparse end-to-end), cargo check clean both targets, cargo test --release -p kovan clean (168+15+17+7 passing), manual CLI smoke test (kovan-cli project regen against a throwaway synthetic project folder) matches the design doc's example schema exactly.

title: kovan: implement kovan.toml auto-generation/maintenance for a 'kovan folder' project

description:
VISCOCHAB is a pure 27-ODE rate system (bibfor/algorith/rkdcha.F90), not a yield surface with a consistency condition, so it shares none of the chaboche module's scalar-collapse architecture. It is a clean next tranche and rkdcha.F90 has been read and understood (parameter map coeft(1..25) to nomc(4..28) verified against cvmmat.F90). BLOCKER NEEDING A MAINTAINER RULING: outram_foam_basic_lib::ode::Rkf45 takes &dyn OdeSystem, a trait object at the call site, which the workspace no-trait-objects rule forbids. Decide whether that boundary coercion is acceptable or whether a typed-state integrator is wanted. Also flagged: likely typo in rkdcha.F90 where da2v uses (1-d1) and symmetry with the da1v line implies (1-d2).

description:
Maintainer sequencing constraint for the HTGR branch, recorded so it is not silently violated.

  - Phase 0 (helium properties, graphite properties) and Phase 1 (neutronics anchors) are LOW RISK and may proceed in parallel as background work.
  - Phase 2 onward (core thermal-hydraulics, coupled steady state, transients, BOP, process heat) must NOT start until the TAMPINES transonic HEM critical-flow V&V item is closed.

Context: the Marviken critical-flow work is live in tampines (marviken_tests.rs, test 23 validated / test 24 explicitly NOT validated and kept as an honest characterisation), and op-ja3t tracks the HEM result landing in tampines-steam-tables.

This bead exists to be checked before anyone opens Phase 2 work, and closed when the gate lifts.
title: HTGR SEQUENCING GATE: Phase 2 onward blocked on TAMPINES transonic HEM critical-flow V&V

description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-14. op-qpgw (Done) added the operator-toggleable degC/K display unit, but HtgrSimApp::display_unit still opens on LegendUnit::default(), which is kelvin (per app/mod.rs's own doc comment on the display_unit field: "its default is kelvin, which is what this simulator displayed before the toggle existed"). Change the opening default to degrees Celsius.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT carried over from op-qpgw, still binding: this is a display-layer-only default. Do not let the changed default touch HtgrSnapshot, PlantCommands, or any correlation/controller/solver input -- it only changes which LegendUnit variant HtgrSimApp::new() picks for the initial self.display_unit.

SCOPE QUESTION carried over from op-qpgw and still open: htgr_sim_v1 only, or should the shared default in the engine's LegendUnit itself change (which would also affect fhr_sim_v2 and any other simulator built on the same widget)? Given op-qpgw scoped the toggle per-simulator (display_unit lives in HtgrSimApp, not in the engine), default this bead to htgr_sim_v1-only unless told otherwise.
title: htgr_sim_v1: default temperature display unit should be degC, not K
